Median and per month: what existing single-family primary-home policies pay, premium plus fees (a new policy is priced at full risk). Insured units: every NFIP policy unit in force on July 31, 2026, including condos, rentals and businesses.

Built from 3,490,299 NFIP policy records and 2,680,429 claim records downloaded from FEMA: every record the download listed for each state, none missing. How we check them

Three things to know first

How fast does it start? Most policies start 30 days after you buy, but there is no wait if you buy it with a new or refinanced mortgage.

Am I required to buy it? Federal law requires it only in a high-risk zone (A or V) with a federally regulated or backed mortgage, or federal help to buy or build (42 U.S.C. §4012a). Outside them, a lender can still require it. In Florida, homes insured by Citizens with wind cover need it in any zone. Check your zone on FEMA's flood map.

Does my homeowners policy cover floods? Standard homeowners insurance does not cover flood damage; flood insurance is bought separately, through the federal NFIP or a private insurer.

Why our prices differ from other sites

These are what existing single-family policies pay today, premium plus fees, as a median (the middle policy). Sites that quote an average premium, a single year, or every policy type get a lower or higher number from the same records. A new policy is priced at FEMA's full-risk rate, often higher; each state page shows both side by side.
